title: General biology I: molecules and cells
stage: College neuroscience and cognitive science degree
audience: a college student in a neuroscience, cognitive science, psychology or biology degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Explain biological molecules, cell structure, membranes, metabolism and enzymes, respiration and photosynthesis, signaling, the cell cycle, meiosis, inheritance, DNA replication and gene expression.

weeks.8: The cell cycle and its regulation

blocks.deliverable: Match each organelle to a disease caused by its failure.
Predict the effect of an inhibitor on an enzyme's rate.
Account for the ATP yield of glucose oxidation.
Week 7 midterm; trace a receptor tyrosine kinase pathway and its link to cancer.
Explain nondisjunction and solve linked-gene problems.
Predict the effect of a mutation on a protein.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Enzyme kinetics with supplied data: compute reaction rates, plot the effects of temperature and pH, and explain the shapes of the curves.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
